questions.q: Why does COPY_HISTORY report on Snowpipe loads, not just manual COPY INTO loads?
options: Snowpipe's automatic loads go through the same underlying load path and get logged the same way
COPY_HISTORY only reports on Snowpipe, never on manual COPY INTO
COPY_HISTORY only works if the pipe is paused
It doesn't — Snowpipe loads require a completely separate function
questions.explain: Because Snowpipe ultimately runs the same load mechanism, COPY_HISTORY reports both manual and Snowpipe-triggered loads consistently.

questions.q: What does it mean if a file never appears in COPY_HISTORY at all, even though you know it landed in the bucket?
options: COPY_HISTORY is broken and needs to be recreated
The pipe never received the trigger for that file — check PIPE_USAGE_HISTORY and the event notification setup instead
The file loaded perfectly and doesn't need to be logged
The file was deleted before Snowflake could see it
questions.explain: COPY_HISTORY only reports on loads that actually started; a file that never triggered the pipe leaves no COPY_HISTORY entry at all, pointing to a trigger problem instead of a parsing problem.

questions.q: What does PIPE_USAGE_HISTORY report on, that COPY_HISTORY does not?
options: The names of every user who has ever queried the target table
The warehouse size used for manual loads
Per-pipe activity — files seen, bytes processed, and credits used over a time window
The exact SQL text of every COPY INTO statement ever run
questions.explain: PIPE_USAGE_HISTORY summarizes a pipe's own activity level, which is the right tool for confirming whether the pipe is receiving events at all.

questions.q: After resuming a paused pipe with ALTER PIPE ... SET PIPE_EXECUTION_PAUSED = FALSE, why might files that arrived during the pause still not load?
options: Paused pipes permanently delete any files that arrive during the pause
Files older than 5 minutes are automatically discarded
The pipe must be dropped and recreated from scratch
Unpausing doesn't retroactively pick up missed files — ALTER PIPE ... REFRESH is needed to re-scan the stage for them
questions.explain: The original trigger event already fired and passed while the pipe was paused, so REFRESH is needed to explicitly re-scan the stage and queue anything missed.

questions.q: According to this lesson, checking SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS first can quickly rule out which common cause of a broken pipe?
options: A paused pipe — executionState: PAUSED points directly at that cause
A permission gap on the target table
A file format mismatch
An ARN mismatch in the S3 event notification
questions.explain: SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS directly reports executionState, so seeing PAUSED immediately identifies that specific cause without further digging.
